options.explanation: A logarithmic extra factor is not polynomially larger than leaf growth, so root domination does not apply.

workedExample:
Identify the parameters and apply the logarithmic-factor extension of the balanced case:

```formula
a = 2,  b = 2,  c = log_2(2) = 1
f(n) = n × (log(n))^1
f(n) = Θ(n^c(log(n))^k)
k = 1
T(n) = Θ(n^c(log(n))^{k+1})
T(n) = Θ(n × (log(n))^2)
where
T(n): the running time on input size n
log_2: the base-2 logarithm; log_2(x) is the power you raise 2 to in order to get x
a: the number of recursive calls
b: the shrink factor
c: the critical exponent log_b(a)
f(n): the work outside the recursive calls
k: the power of log n in f(n)
n: the input size
log: the base-2 logarithm
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constants
In words: the outside work matches the leaf count n times one power of log n, so case 2 adds one more power of log n.
```

Each level has more nodes but smaller inputs. Their linear factors cancel, leaving the original input size times a logarithm that decreases by one per level. The card sums those internal-level contributions; fixed-base-case leaves add only linear work:

```formula
T(n) ≈ n × (L + (L − 1) + … + 1)
T(n) ≈ n L × (L + 1) / 2
L = log_2(n)
T(n) = Θ(n × (log(n))^2)
N_j = 2^j, s_j = n/2^j
w_j = s_j log_2(s_j)
N_j w_j = n(log_2(n) − j)
where
T(n): the total work in the tree
n: the input size
L: the number of levels, log_2(n)
j: the level number, from 0 at the root
log_2(n): the base-2 logarithm of n
log: the base-2 logarithm
…: "and so on" down to 1
≈: approximately equal to; the displayed sum counts internal-node work, with a further linear leaf cost for a fixed positive base case
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constants
N_j: the number of level-j nodes
log_2: the base-2 logarithm
s_j: the size per level-j node
w_j: one node’s outside work
In words: the level totals fall by n each level, from n × L down to n, and that arithmetic series adds up to about half of n × L squared.
```
